description: The Icelandic civil protection department publishes a page on volcanic hazard on the Reykjanes peninsula that presents reports from a larger hazard and risk assessment project for the peninsula led by the Icelandic Meteorological Office, with a link to download the reports and a list of questions and answers. The assessment covers lava flow, earthquakes, gas pollution and tephra fall, and the page says the capital area of seven municipalities lies largely in an area that such activity could affect, as could municipalities on Reykjanes and in western South Iceland. The reports assess the exposure of critical infrastructure: power plants including Hellisheiði and Nesjavellir and important transmission lines lie partly in or near areas exposed to lava flow, and hot water for the capital area comes from several sources and routes, so the reports are used to assess backup routes, mitigation and strengthening of pipelines and water sources. More reports will be added as the project continues. Access is free online; no licence is stated. Caveats: the reports are long-term hazard assessments for planning, the page says they do not indicate imminent danger, and the content is in Icelandic. Coverage is the Reykjanes peninsula and the capital area. It supports hazard exposure and cascading failure analysis of energy, district heating and water systems; related records are the Icelandic infrastructure asset inventory and the Reykjanes volcanic hazard map of the Met Office.
